CHARGES U/S 120B IPC, 420 r/w 120B IPC AND SECTION 12 PASSPORTS ACT AGAINST ACCUSED/REVISIONISTS SUMIT SACHHAR AND ASHISH SHARMA.

ORDER:
1. Revisionists have filed present revision petition challenging the impugned order dated 26.05.2022 whereby Ld. CMM West had framed charges against them under the Sections mentioned above.
2. Revisionists Sumit Sachhar and Ashish Sharma are accused 3 and 4 respectively before Ld. Trial Court.

Two other accused persons namely Ulhas Prabhakar Khaire and Raksha J Urs were also chargesheeted as accused no. 1 and 2 before Ld. Trial Court and charges were also framed against Sumit Sachar vs State on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88681545/
1 them vide impugned order dated 26.05.2022 but they have not challenged the impugned order.
State has been impleaded as Respondent in the present revision petition.
For the sake of convenience, parties shall be referred to by their nomenclature before Ld. Trial Court.
3. Arguments on the revision petition heard.
Record carefully perused.

BRIEF FACTS:
4. Brief facts of the case necessary for disposal of the present revision petition are that the present FIR was registered on a complaint dated 07.12.2012 made by Inspector Raj Kumar Saha, EOW,
Crime Branch with the allegations that while he was investigating case FIR No. 84/2011 and 152/2011 PS Moti Nagar u/s 406/419/420/467/468/471/120B/34 IPC, it was revealed that Ulhas Prabhakar Khaire had got a passport no. J-4078239 dated 07.10.2010 issued from Delhi impersonating himself as Lokeshwar Dev.

His wife Raksha J Urs also obtained passport no.
J-4078244 dated 07.10.2010 from Delhi impersonating as Priyanka Saraswat Dev.
They had also got issued passports in the name of their daughters Gungun Dev and Gunjan bearing passport numbers J-4078240 dated 07.10.2010 and J-4078245 dated 07.10.2010.
These passports were got issued by them by using fraudulent means and misrepresentation of facts.

During the PC remand, accused Ulhas disclosed that he had got these passports issued from Delhi with the help of accused Sumit Sacchar and Ashish Sharma, partners of Global Destination Management, RG Complex, Sector 14 Rohini, Delhi.

Accordingly, the investigation of FIR No. 84/2011 has revealed that accused Ulhas Prabhakar Khaire and Raksha J Urs got issued the said passports by fraudulent means and misrepresentation of facts in connivance with Sumit Sachhar and Ashish Sharma.

Accordingly,
complaint was made for initiating appropriate actions against them.
5. On the basis of this complaint, FIR No. 167/2012 PS EOW was registered u/s 419/420/467/468/471/120B/34 IPC and Section 12 Passports Act, 1967.

6. After investigation, chargesheet was filed against 4 accused persons namely Ulhas Prabhakar Khaire (A-1), Raksha J Urs (A-2), Sumit Sachhar (A-3) and Ashish Sharma (A-4) u/s 419/420/467/468/471/120B/34 IPC and Section 12 Passports Act, 1967.
7. Three Accused persons namely Surinder Kumar @ Surinder Singh, SI Ranbir Singh and Seema Raj were kept in Column no. 12 as the investigation against them was stated to be pending.
Out of these 3 accused persons, Accused Surinder Singh @ Surinder Kumar has already been declared a PO and supplementary chargesheet qua him was filed before Ld. Trial Court on 09.03.2017.

IMPUGNED ORDER:
8.

After hearing the arguments on the point of charge, Ld. Trial Court held vide impugned order dated 26.05.2022 that a prima facie case u/s 120B/420 IPC and Section 12 Passports Act was made out against all the accused persons and prima facie case u/s 120B/419/420/467/468/471 IPC was made out against accused Ulhas Prabhakar and Raksha J Urs.
Charges were framed accordingly, on 26.05.2022 to which the accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

Matter is at the stage Sumit Sachar vs State on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88681545/
2 of recording of prosecution evidence.

sentences.text: GROUNDS OF REVISION:

9. The impugned order on charge has been challenged by accused Sumit Sacchar and Ashish Sharma/Revisionists herein on the ground that the impugned order is bad in law and is not based on proper appreciation of facts and circumstances spelled out in the chargesheet.

Ld. Trial court has failed to appreciate that the revisionists were merely Travel Agents and could not have verified the authenticity of the documents given to them by A-1 and A-2 for getting their passports issued.

Ld.
Trial Court has failed to appreciate the fact that the revisionists were never aware about the actual names of A-1 and A-2 who had already assumed the fictitious names of Lokeshwar Dev and Priyanka before meeting the revisionists and had also procured fake identity documents regarding their fictitious names.
The revisionists had no occasions to discover that A-1 and A-2 were impersonating as Lokeshwar Dev and Priyanka.

Ms. Seema Raj, Income Tax Commissioner had issued verification certificates for issuance of passports in favour of A-1 and A-2, however, she has been given a clean chit and has not been chargesheeted by the IO.

Similarly, after issuance of the passport on tatkal basis, police verification of A-1 and A-2 in respect of the submitted ID and address proofs was made by ASI Ranbir Singh who had submitted that all the documents were verified.
Even, he has not been chargesheeted by the IO for the reasons best known to him.

Once, Ms. Seema Raj and ASI Ranbir Singh who had verified the identity documents of A-1 and A-2 prepared in the impersonated names have not been chargesheeted, it is apparent on record that the revisionists herein have been made a scapegoat and chargesheeted for merely processing the passport documents of A-1 and A-2 and providing them services as a travel agent only.

No evidence has been produced on record to show that the revisionists were aware about the real identity of A-1 and A-2 or had deliberately assisted them in obtaining fake documents under impersonated names or getting the passport issued in the impersonated names.
Being a travel agent, it was not the duty of the revisionists to verify the identity documents furnished by A-1 and A-2.
The revisionists had merely provided the services of a travel agent to A-1 and A-2 and their other employees and obtained their legitimate fees as travel agents.

There is no document on record to suggest that the revisionist had any role to play in the other scams committed by A-1 and A-2 and thus, there is no element of criminal conspiracy on record, nor the revisionists can be held liable for the offence of cheating as charged against them.
Apart from the disclosure statements of A-1 and A-2, there is no other evidence to connect the revisionists with the alleged offence of cheating.

Thus, there is no prima facie case u/s 120B/420 IPC or Section 12 Passports Act made out against the accused persons namely Sumit Sachhar and Ashish Sharma and accordingly, they are entitled to discharge in the present case.
ARGUMENTS OF LD. ADDITIONAL PP FOR THE STATE:
10.
Per contra, the revision petition is strongly opposed on behalf of the State.
It has been argued by Ld.
Additional PP for the State assisted by the IO

that the case of the prosecution against the revisionist is not that they were aware that A-1 and A- 2 were getting passports issued in fake names by impersonating as Lokeshwar Dev and Priyanka Saraswat Dev.

On the other hand, the allegations against the revisionists are that they had conspired Sumit Sachar vs State on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88681545/
3 to get the passports issued for A-1 and A-2 by fraudulent means.

sentences.text: They played a crucial role in obtaining of the passports and duly followed up for the said purpose with the relevant authorities.
Various records have been seized by the IO during investigation from the office of the revisionists in support of these allegations.
They had got the certificates of verification issued in favour of A-1 and A-2 from Ms. Seema Raj by representing that A-1 and A-2 were known to them.

Accused Ashish Sharma had even represented that Priyanka Saraswat was his sister and thus, not only conspired but also acted in pursuance of the conspiracy to get the passports issued for A-1 and A-2 by fraudulent means.
There are independent public witnesses examined by the IO who have stated about these misrepresentations.

In addition to this, accused Surinder Singh (since PO) had also got a fake passport issued by changing his name to Surinder Kumar and his affidavit of change of name was attested by the revisionists which clearly show a conspiracy between the accused persons for issuance of passports by fraudulent means.

11. During investigation, it has also come on record that substantial money has been received by the revisionists herein from A-1 and A-2 in their bank accounts in pursuance of a criminal conspiracy and for getting the passports issued by fraudulent means.
Accordingly, clearly a prima facie case u/s 120B/420 IPC and Section 12 Passport Act is made out against both the accused persons and charges have been rightly framed against them.

Even otherwise, impugned order is a well reasoned and detailed order passed after considering all the material available on record and due discussion of the entire evidence collected during investigation.
There is no infirmity or illegality in the impugned order, neither any has been pointed out by Ld. Counsel for the revisionist.

Accordingly,
there is no reason to interfere with the impugned order dated 26.05.2022 and thus, dismissal of the present revision petition is prayed.

FINDINGS:
12.
I have heard the submissions made and carefully perused the record as well as the statements of various witnesses recorded by the IO during investigation.

13. The scope of enquiry, a judge is required to make while considering the question of framing of charges has been considered by the Apex Court in Union of India Vs. Prafulla Kumar Samal and Anr. (1979) 3 SCC 4.

entities.text: Union of India Vs. Prafulla Kumar Samal and Anr. (1979) 3 SCC 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
After an exhaustive survey of the case law on the point, the Apex court has laid down the following principles:-
" (1) That the Judge while considering the question of framing the charges under section 227 of the Code has the undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out.

(2) Where the materials placed before the Court disclose grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly explained the Court will be, fully justified in framing a charge and proceeding with the trial.
(3) The test to determine a prima facie case would be naturally depend upon the facts of each case and it is difficult to lay down a rule of universal application.

By and large however, if two views are equally possible and the Judge is satisfied that the evidence Sumit Sachar vs State on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88681545/
4 produced before him while giving rise to some suspicion but not grave suspicion against the accused, he will be fully within his right to discharge the accused.

entities.text:
Sumit Sachar vs State on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88681545/
4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (4) That in exercising his jurisdiction under section 227 of the Code the Judge which under the present Code is a senior and experienced Judge cannot act merely as a Post Office or a mouth-piece of the prosecution, but has to consider the broad probabilities of the case, the total effect of the evidence and the documents produced before the Court, any basic infirmities appearing in the case and so on.

This however,
does not mean that the Judge should make a roving enquiry into the pros and cons of the matter and weigh the evidence as if he was conducting a trial."
14. Considering the overall material available on record, no infirmity or illegality is found in the impugned order dated 26.05.2022.
The impugned order dated 26.05.2022 is a detailed and well reasoned order passed after considering all the materials and allegations against various accused persons.

A bare perusal of order dated 26.05.2022 clearly shows that it has not been passed in a routine manner but after considering the allegations and evidence against each and every accused person and giving detailed reasons for directing framing of charges.

15. I do not find any merit in the arguments of Ld. Counsel for the revisionists that since there is no evidence on record to show that the revisionists were aware that A-1 and A-2 were impersonating themselves as Lokeshwar Dev and Priyanka Saraswat Dev, they cannot be charged for offences of conspiracy or cheating.

This is so as the case of the prosecution against the revisionists herein is that they had conspired with co-accused persons for getting passports issued for them by fraudulent means and have received consideration for the said services provided by them.

Neither the prosecution has alleged that the revisionists herein had assisted A-1 and A-2 in obtaining fake documents/ID proofs under impersonated names, nor the accused persons have been charged for the said offence.
Accordingly, this argument of Ld. Defence Counsel does not inspire the confidence of the Court.

16. As regards the conspiracy between the revisionists herein and A-1 and A-2, it is apparent on record considering the evidences showing their involvement in getting verification certificate for A-1 and A-2 issued from a Gazzetted Officer by misrepresenting facts, the evidence in the form of data collected from the computers seized from their office as well as evidence in the form of money received by the revisionists from the Firm of A-1 and A-2.

The statements of witnesses Prashant Kapoor and Abhiraj clearly show that the revisionist herein had introduced A-1 and A-2 as their close relatives and family members to Ms. Seema Raj in order to procure the verification certificate for issuanace of their passports.
Accordingly, from the material on record, a prima facie case u/s 120B IPC; 420 r/w 120B IPC and Section 12 Passports Act is clearly made out against accused Sumit Sachhar and Ashish Sharma.
No infirmity or illegality is observed in the impugned order dated 26.05.2022 or the charge framed against the revisionists.
17. In view of the reasons given above, I find no merit in the present revision petition.
The same is accordingly, dismissed and the impugned order dated 26.05.2022 is upheld.
